excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
paraphrase: A three-month cadence had forced teams to prioritize evaluation frequency over comprehensiveness and methodology improvement.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6x buffer), with more general requirements to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
paraphrase: Specific prior methodology elements (e.g., 1% compute for elicitation, 6x buffer) were replaced with general requirements to match adversary effort and estimate future capability impacts.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Evaluation science is not yet mature enough to confidently prescribe a precise buffer between current models and a Capability Threshold, though this remains an aspiration.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: More outcome-focused safeguard requirements: We have updated our ASL-3 safeguards requirements to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.
paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were updated to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them.
paraphrase: Instead of detailing specific safeguards, overall security/deployment standards and their requirements are now specified.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
paraphrase: The outcome-focused approach allows more flexible safeguard adaptation as understanding improves.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models: We have clarified which actors are in and out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: The scope of actors covered by the ASL-3 Security Standard was clarified.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: We also removed the commitment to protect against scaled attacks and distillation attacks from the ASL-2 Security standard.
paraphrase: The commitment to protect against scaled and distillation attacks was removed from the ASL-2 Security Standard.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: While distillation remains a concern for more capable models, models stored under ASL-2 safeguards have not yet reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Distillation remains a concern for more capable models, but ASL-2 models have not reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard was updated to allow safeguard levels to vary by deployment context.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: For any general access systems, we still require passing intensive red-teaming. For internal use, safety testing and deployments to sufficiently trusted users, we will instead require a combination of access controls and monitoring.
paraphrase: General access systems still require intensive red-teaming, while internal use and trusted-user deployments instead require access controls and monitoring.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: New Capability and Safeguards Reports: We have introduced Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports.
paraphrase: Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports were newly introduced.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: We expect that aggregating all the available evidence about model capabilities will provide decision makers with a more complete picture of the overall level of risk and improve our ability to solicit feedback on our work.
paraphrase: Aggregating capability evidence is expected to give decision-makers a fuller risk picture and improve feedback-seeking.

locator: Changelog / October 15, 2024 / Internal and external accountability
excerpt: Internal and external accountability: We have made a number of changes to our previous "procedural commitments." These include expanding the duties of the Responsible Scaling Officer; adding internal critique and external expert input on capability and safeguard assessments; new procedures related to internal governance;
paraphrase: Procedural commitments were changed to expand RSO duties, add internal/external review input, and introduce new internal governance procedures.
